title: Pathology networks identify gastric-cancer lymph-node metastases
summary: A cascade of Faster R-CNN/DeepLab and fused Xception/DenseNet models analyzed lymph-node slides from 222 gastric-cancer patients. In the reported 327-slide test cohort from 94 patients, metastasis classification had positive and negative predictive values of 93.53% and 97.99%. This is a single-center archival clinical validation; the paper’s “prospective” terminology does not establish a new frozen-model clinical trial. Poorly differentiated and scattered tumor cells were more often missed, and no improved patient outcome was demonstrated.
ai_technology: Faster R-CNN; DeepLab; fused Xception and DenseNet-121
organization: Peking University Cancer Hospital; Tsinghua University

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full relevant cohort/reference, model and validation Methods, Results and discussion; supplementary materials not inspected. Publisher canonical front DOI/title and online date verified. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Pathology-reference classification of lymph-node metastases in archival 2009–2019 gastric-cancer slides. The source describes 594 training slides and 327 test slides, with reported test-cohort PPV 93.53% and NPV 97.99%; these are not patient-level screening-benefit estimates.
evidence.unknown: External-center generalization, prospective frozen-model performance and patient benefit remain unestablished. The Methods alternate image-random-split and patient-cohort descriptions, leaving the exact grouping of repeated slides incompletely documented. Hard-to-distinguish histological subtypes had more false negatives.
evidence.ai_role: Faster R-CNN/DeepLab locate and segment lymph nodes; fused Xception/DenseNet learned features classify metastatic tissue against expert pathology labels.
